evidence: The shell derives its numbered primary order from the exact persisted Research Intent workflow profile returned by Core; editing an unsaved profile form does not change navigation, while a successful persisted revision does.

The navigation model exposes explicit complete, current, upcoming, attention, optional, and cyclical presentations without treating a route visit as durable completion. Because T04 owns durable workflow-state mutation, T03 consumes only explicit authoritative state and otherwise renders the conservative current/upcoming projection.
Unimplemented future stages remain visible but disabled and have no invented reference routes; all profile-specific stage labels come from the authenticated Core catalog projection.
The secondary All tools surface identifies pages outside the ordered workflow as supporting tools and retains the complete implemented tool inventory independently of profile order.

Opening a supporting tool preserves an exact return witness containing project ID/root, Research Intent revision/hash, catalog version/hash, selected profile, primary stage, and primary page; one return action restores that exact primary context.
Changing any bound workflow or project identity invalidates the stale return witness rather than silently returning to a substituted context.

The navigation is operable with semantic buttons, current-step indication, labeled primary/supporting regions, visible focus, keyboard traversal, and a direct return action; focused renderer and browser checks cover these paths.

The adaptive rail becomes a horizontal workflow strip at the approved breakpoint while preserving order, context, controls, and reachability; built-frame checks cover desktop and narrow viewports in light and dark themes.

The task UI contract binds the changed shell, Intent integration, navigation component, and model to the approved Academic Minimal v1.5 reference and passes the repository UI gate plus workflow and accessibility conformance suites.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: T03 changes a governed desktop navigation boundary fed by a public Core catalog projection and persisted Research Intent identity. Credible failures include trusting a partial or substituted catalog, deriving navigation from unsaved UI state, treating visits as completion, losing access to supporting tools, returning to a stale project/profile/revision, inventing routes for future stages, and breaking keyboard, responsive, theme, or approved-reference behavior. The selected checks therefore cover exact generated-client projection authentication, model and rendered-component state transitions, persisted-selection integration, production assembly, built-frame browser inspection, governed UI/reference/accessibility contracts, changed-file Python quality, exact affected-path selection, and repository governance. The full profile was also sampled and its only failures were proven in unchanged formatter/type-check paths, which remain explicit W1-exit debt.
deferred: The affected selector assigns desktop performance to the complete W1-exit matrix; T03 changes no approved performance threshold.
